import pandas as pd

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_81/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_81/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_81/training_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_81/training_3.csv"

# Step 1: Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df_source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)
df_source3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)

# Step 2: UNION operation on Source3_81_1, Source3_81_2, Source3_81_3
# They share the same schema, so union (concat) is valid
union_of_Source3_81_1_2_3 = pd.concat([df_source1, df_source2, df_source3], ignore_index=True)

# Step 3: JOIN operation between Source3_81_0 and the union result on 'id'
# Ensure 'id' column exists in both dataframes and is used as join key
# Use inner join to keep only matching keys as typical for such join
df_target = pd.merge(df_source0, union_of_Source3_81_1_2_3, on="id", suffixes=('', '_union'))

# Step 4: The target schema matches the source schema exactly, so no column renaming needed
# But after join, columns from union have suffix '_union' - we need to resolve duplicates
# According to the operation, the join is on 'id' only, so all other columns from union are duplicates
# We keep columns from df_source0 and drop the duplicated columns from union side except 'id'

# Columns to keep from union side: only 'id' (already present), drop all others with '_union' suffix
columns_to_drop = [col for col in df_target.columns if col.endswith('_union')]
df_target.drop(columns=columns_to_drop, inplace=True)

# Step 5: Ensure data types match target schema exactly
# Target schema types:
# categories: string (can be list or string, keep as is)
# commentCount: integer
# completed: boolean
# copyright: integer
# cover: string
# cover_timestamp: string
# createDate: string
# deleted: boolean
# description: string
# firstPartId: integer
# firstPublishedPart.createDate: string
# firstPublishedPart.id: integer
# id: integer
# language.id: integer
# language.name: string
# lastPublishedPart.createDate: string
# lastPublishedPart.id: integer
# length: integer
# mature: boolean
# modifyDate: string
# numParts: integer
# parts: string
# rating: integer
# readCount: integer
# tags: string
# title: string
# url: string
# user.avatar: string
# user.fullname: string
# user.name: string
# voteCount: integer

# Convert columns to appropriate types
# For booleans, ensure dtype is bool
bool_cols = ['completed', 'deleted', 'mature']
for col in bool_cols:
    if col in df_target.columns:
        df_target[col] = df_target[col].astype(bool)

# For integer columns, convert to Int64 to allow NA if any
int_cols = ['commentCount', 'copyright', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.id', 'id',
            'language.id', 'lastPublishedPart.id', 'length', 'numParts', 'rating', 'readCount', 'voteCount']
for col in int_cols:
    if col in df_target.columns:
        df_target[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_target[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# For string columns, convert to string and fill NaN with empty string if needed
str_cols = ['categories', 'cover', 'cover_timestamp', 'createDate', 'description',
            'firstPublishedPart.createDate', 'language.name', 'lastPublishedPart.createDate',
            'modifyDate', 'parts', 'tags', 'title', 'url', 'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name']
for col in str_cols:
    if col in df_target.columns:
        df_target[col] = df_target[col].astype(str).fillna('')

# Step 6: Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_81/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
